title: Introducing Memory
format_note: Calm 81 s explainer for one feature: black title cards alternate with white redrawn-UI scenes, no voiceover, ends on a tagline and logo.
one_thing: Harvey remembers what you tell it, and the film shows that by lighting memory cells in the colour of each highlighted phrase.

transcript.voice_style: No speech. Whisper returned only 'Transcribed by' hallucinations, so the film is music plus on-screen text.
transcript.script_shape: Three claims in on-screen text: Harvey Learns From Your Actions; And Uses its Memory to Improve its Answers; You Reason, Harvey Remembers. Tagline closes.

structure.frame0: Per the strip (window-01) the frame is near-black until 0.4 s, then a lone white serif H centred; f0001.jpg shows the H alone. No product in frame.
structure.first_3s: H on black to 2.2 s, then a grey card with concentric rectangles and a small H slides in at the H's position, cut at 2.97 s to the full card on white.

beats.what: Lone white H on near-black, silent for the first 0.4 s.
Card with concentric rectangles slides in over the H, then sits on white ground.
Card flips apart into six letter tiles spelling MEMORY.
Black card: Harvey Learns From Your Actions, fading in word by word.
Empty Ask Harvey composer; a prompt is typed: Draft a letter requesting an extension on the due diligence review period.
Prompt slides left; concise and direct highlight teal; grid cells light; Memory Stored chip at 22 s.
Second prompt about the Acme stock purchase agreement; buyer and target facts highlight rose and store as cells.
Black card: And Uses its Memory to Improve its Answers.
New prompt; Searching Memory lists the stored preferences, highlights matching the grid colours; Memory Used chip at 52 s.
Two more prompts (Smith v. Johnson, liability cap) each pull stored facts; grid ends multicoloured.
You Reason in black, Harvey Remembers in grey beneath.
Card flips back to MEMORY tiles; Never Start From Scratch Again. and H below.

hero_moment.what: Memory Used chip appears while Searching Memory phrases highlight in the same teal and rose as the stored grid cells (f0027.jpg).

ending.what: MEMORY tiles with the tagline above and a small H below, held to the end; audio silent from 78.9 s.

rhythm.how_change_is_paced: Seven hard cuts, four of them black/white inversions at title cards. The longest shot runs 33.17 s (41% of runtime) with UI state changing about every 2 s (median_hold_s 2.15). No burst.

look.ground: Near-white (#fafafa-ish) UI scenes against near-black title cards; 92.5% of sampled frames light, 7.5% dark (dark_share 0.075).
look.accent_use: Pastel teal, rose and lilac mark phrases and matching grid cells; the second line Harvey Remembers is set in grey as the only type accent.
look.type: Title cards in a high-contrast serif, Title Case; UI in a clean grotesque, bold for user prompts, grey for agent steps.

look.depth: Flat. A slight 3D perspective tilt on the card and tiles during flips (strips window-03 and window-32); otherwise no shadows or depth.

product_ui.camera_on_ui: Static, no zoom. The composer is centred, then the prompt panel shifts left to make room for a 6x6 grid of memory cells.
product_ui.notes: Prompt text at t=52 is 16-18 px ink height on 720 (about 2.2-2.5%), under the 2.6% floor. Chips Memory Stored and Memory Used are about 14 px. Colour highlights carry the meaning when text is too small.

motion.ui_motion: Highlight bars grow behind phrases, then matching grid cells tint; chips fade in and out at the top of the grid; the grid scatters and reforms at 36 s (f0019).
motion.camera: No camera moves. Card and tiles flip in 3D (window-03, window-32) for about 0.3 s.
motion.eases: Not measured. The card flip and slide read as smooth decelerations in the strips, but easing curves were not fitted.

H centred on black cuts to card corner with small H in the same spot.
Card flips apart into letter tiles that spell MEMORY.

Memory Used chip and highlights appear when the agent searches memory.

on_screen_lines.text: Draft a letter requesting an extension on the due diligence review period. Keep it concise and direct.
What are the key considerations for a stock purchase agreement where the seller is retaining certain liabilities? For context, I'm representing the buyer...
And Uses its Memory to Improve its Answers
For the Acme stock purchase matter, draft a memo summarizing the top risks.
Searching Memory: User prefers concise and direct language; Acme is a Delaware C-Corp and you are representing the buyer
Draft interrogatory responses for the Smith v. Johnson case; Primary data custodians are in Sales and Finance; Time period for damages is 2019-2021
Draft talking points to push back on liability cap; Uncapped indemnity requires GC approval and previously negotiated 3x cap

good.observation: Highlight colours on prompt phrases match the tint of cells in the memory grid, so a viewer can see which phrase was stored without a caption.
The same card-to-MEMORY flip opens and closes the film, so the ending reads as a return rather than a new scene.
good.evidence: strips window-03 and window-32; f0004, f0039

good.observation: Three claim cards on black separate the product scenes in time with cuts; the white UI scenes then show each claim happening.
Proof repeats the same layout three times with a new prompt, so memory recall is seen to recur rather than asserted once.
Tagline holds 3.9 s with MEMORY tiles and H, longer than the 2 s minimum.
The legal prompts are specific (Acme, Delaware C-corp, 3x cap, 2019-2021), which makes the remembered facts credible.

weak.observation: Agent-step text and chips are small for a phone screen; the Searching Memory lines are the proof and they are the smallest type.

weak.observation: Frame 0 is a lone logo on black and the first 0.4 s is black and silent; the product subject arrives at 2.2 s.
Cuts are not tied to the music; the score has no beat to land on.
Long stretches of near-identical UI (static share 0.667) give little visual change; the 33 s shot relies on small highlight changes.

rule_candidates.rule: Colour-code the stored information: give each highlighted phrase a tint and light a matching cell in a persistent diagram, so cause and effect are visible without extra copy.
Between worlds, hard-cut on a polarity flip (white UI to black claim card) instead of dissolving; the film does this 4 times in 81 s.
A single-line claim card may exceed 6 words if it stays one line at 5-6% of frame height; the 8-word card read cleanly at 43 px on 720.
A calm explainer can run one continuous UI shot of 30 s or more if something visibly changes every 2 s; judge pacing by change events, not cuts.
Prove a feature by repeating one scene layout three times with a new input each time; keep the layout fixed so only the content changes.
Open and close on the same object: a flip that turns the hero object into the title tiles at 4 s and again at 76.5 s, then hold the tagline 3.9 s.
Keep agent-step text at or above 2.6% of the short side (19 px on 720); this film's 16-18 px lines in the proof beat fall below it.
rule_candidates.evidence: ink measure t=52: 16 and 18 px; f0026.jpg

rule_candidates.rule: A quiet beatless film does not need cuts on music; but state this and drop the sync check (share 0.0 vs chance 0.125) rather than force a hero on a score peak.
